open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove conclusions \({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\) for the face-robust three-coordinate prior: an exact-target Bayes-risk expansion uniform over \(\mathcal L_n\), \(\mathcal X_n\), and \(\mathcal Z_n\), together with one computable common tail and a computable all-future primal tail that does not use \(B_{c^\dagger}\) as program data.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact nested-posterior decomposition in the partial result removes the earlier loose covariance bound, but it leaves the Bayes risk of the data-dependent regression \(m_\lambda(O)=\mathbb E[M\mid\lambda,O]\). The declared Fisher-information identity controls the latent coordinate \(\alpha_nx\), not this regression, whose observed-cell corrections interact with the order-\(n^{-4/3}\) residual term. No frozen result supplies the needed target-specific expansion uniformly over local \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation perturbations, the positive-count exterior, and zero-count faces. Exact evaluation at each \(n\) supplies no computable all-future modulus. On the primal side the only analytic majorant contains the existential constant \(B_{c^\dagger}\), which is not computable input to \(\mathsf E\).
open_obligations.attempted: I retained the live three-coordinate face guards, verified the diagonal positivity and denominator bounds from the monotone ledger, used the exact orbit reduction, and derived the nested conditional-variance formula by representing the multinomial-plus-orbit prior as independent labeled response types conditional on the tube coordinate. I evaluated its first term by exact binary regression and the eight response types, obtaining the stated conditional target variance. This identifies rather than discards every second-order target-fluctuation contribution. Applying scalar directional van Trees only to \(\alpha_nx\) still controls the wrong second projection term; pointwise ordered-algebraic enumeration still cannot certify all later sample sizes; and the existing fixed-design remainder still has no computable numerical majorant.
